recipes.name: Jessica's Steak Oscar
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 packet dry Bearnaise sauce mix (such as Knorr®)

steps.text: Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source. Sprinkle the filets with salt and pepper.
Melt 1/4 cup of butter in a small saucepan over low heat; gently stir in crab meat and simmer while you broil the beef filets.

Broil steaks until they reach the desired stage of doneness; for medium (slightly pink in the center), broil 10 to 12 minutes on the first side and 6 minutes on the second side. Set steaks aside to rest.

Place a steamer insert into a skillet, and fill with water to just below the bottom of the steamer. Cover, and bring the water to a boil over high heat. Add asparagus, recover, and steam until just tender, 2 to 6 minutes depending on thickness.

Whisk Bearnaise sauce mix with milk in a saucepan. Add 1/2 cup of butter, and bring the sauce to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly; reduce heat to a simmer, and whisk until sauce has thickened, about 1 minute.
To assemble, top each broiled steak filet with crab meat, then half of the asparagus. Spoon Bearnaise sauce to taste over asparagus and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Jessica's Steak Oscar
raw_recipe.description: Steak Oscar is an elegant dish of beef tenderloin filets topped with buttery crab meat, asparagus, and Bearnaise sauce that's perfect for a special date, Valentine's Day, or just because!

review.reviewBody: Great recipe. Lovely combination. If you can get tarragon, make the Bearnaise sauce yourself; it's so much better than a package.

If you must use packaged sauce mix, Wagners is by far the best. Also, try using jumbo lump crab, it makes the world of difference. I added some deep fried spaghetti noodles for a fun garnish. This recipe is a classic, and a keeper.
Simple, elegant, beautiful and above all else a delicious show stopper! I served this with long grain and wild rice! Thanks for sharing Jessica!

This was delicious. Obviously I used many more pieces of asparagus but we like it. :-) I also used imitation crab because real chunk was $25 for a few ounces. The plate in the picture looks distorted because the site insists on a 960X960 picture. Sorry.

Delicious! Anything with crabmeat is a good idea - so adding it to the filet was amazing. I had never tried bearnaise sauce, but the creamy, rich flavor complemented the steak well and was also delicious on the asparagus! Step 3 doesn't mention how long to simmer the crab in the butter (besides saying to do it while you broil the filets). Since it's already cooked, I simmered it on low in the butter for about 10 minutes. I used a sheet pan with aluminum foil to broil the filets. My oven got extremely smokey within about six minutes of broiling (10 was recommended on first side), so I had to move the oven rack down which added a little more cooking time, but prevented my kitchen from getting smokey. Despite the adjustment, the filets were still juicy and delicious, cooked to a medium temperature.

I was a little skeptical about using a packaged béarnaise sauce recipe, so I used the microwave recipe on All Recipes. I also cooked the steak on the grill but did not add extra smoke. It all turned out very good.
I used the blender hollandaise sauce from this web site (with a bouillon cube added) and this came out great! Thank you for the easy recipe.

Excellent. Used a thick NY strip steak on sale and imitation crab because of price. Only other change was a gentle sprinkle of Old Bay as I sautéed the crab. I prepared the sauce, crab, and asparagus and kept warm as I grilled the steak medium rare. My wife loved it.

Used these exact ingredients although I changed the order of assembly considerably, since we like our steaks rare, it wouldn’t be good to have them sitting so long. I made the Bernaise sauce first, then stir fried the asparagus in garlic butter and when all was ready, we BBQ the steaks. Our company raves about the steaks as well. Sublime! Thank you for a great recipe.

This steak Oscar is similar to a recipe I did a few years ago for Christmas only I used crawfish etouffee. The concept of the recipe is great and it makes a beautiful holiday meal with a nice bread on the side. I would suggest adding some lemon to the crab and maybe some garlic powder along with salt and pepper to the steaks because I thought it was a little bland. Otherwise, my family seemed to have loved it. Plates were clean as a whistle when they were done.
OMG it was fantastic I can’t believe I made it. A definite favorite. I added some shrimp.

Made 4/18/25 and 3.5 stars but I’m rounding up. In my younger years, as a new chef, I would have raved about this; how date night quality it is. It IS good!! And we enjoyed! And for a new cook or, a date night cook pressed for time, this is good! But, this has a lot going on and not a ton of flavor. In a single bite, it as hard to discern the crab from the beef from the asparagus. But!! I also liked how this recipe was a full complete meal. Enjoyed! Thanks Jessica!
Skipping the Asparagus to put some Yams or Rice on the side. Crusty Buttered Toast and a nice Varietal such as Cabernet Sauvignon or Southern Sweet Tea to polish everything off. JMHO.🥩🍠🍠🍚🍞🍷🍵B.W.
OMG That’s all I can say. 🤤
I gave this five stars, but I have not tried it. It looks delicious however when I saw that it was almost 1300 cal I decided I would not make it.
I was looking for a veal Oscar recipe and found this. I used veal cutlet and it was hit!
added a little half and half to the sauce, which thickened it up nicely! everyone loved it!
